curation.lead:
MGX Fund Management Limited is an Abu Dhabi-based artificial intelligence and technology investment vehicle established March 12, 2024 by G42 and Mubadala Investment Company under the Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council, with a target of $100 billion in assets under management [Finding #11220]. The entity is chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE National Security Adviser and brother of UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed, who simultaneously chairs ADIA, ADQ, IHC, First Abu Dhabi Bank, and G42 [Finding #4006]. Khaldoon Khalifa Al Mubarak — Mubadala MD/CEO and concurrent chair of ADCB, Aldar, FAB, MBZUAI, and the Abu Dhabi Executive Affairs Authority — serves as Vice Chairman [Finding #11203]. MGX's SEC Form ADV (CRD 334247) discloses a dual ownership chain: the Mubadala chain runs from the Government of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi through Mubadala, Mamoura Diversified Global Holding, and MIC Industrial Investment 2 RSC LTD; the parallel chain runs through G42 Holding via GX Investments LTD [Finding #3997].

Within its first two years of operation, MGX participated in the largest US technology infrastructure transactions of the period. On the Stargate joint venture, the equity allocation reported by The Information places SoftBank at approximately 40 percent and OpenAI at approximately 40 percent, with Oracle and MGX each contributing approximately $7 billion in initial commitments — a substantially smaller participation than the headline $500 billion figure implies for any individual partner [Finding #11216]. The Stargate-MGX venture and the Klein-Altman-Oklo cluster are, according to the SEC primary-source filings, structurally separate transactions that press treatment has frequently merged [Finding #11236]. Other major MGX deployments include a $2 billion investment in Binance settled via the World Liberty Financial USD1 stablecoin in May 2025 [Finding #3837], an approximately 15 percent stake in the TikTok US restructuring [Finding #4009], participation in Anthropic's $30 billion Series G [Finding #4009], and the $40 billion BlackRock-led acquisition of Aligned Data Centers [Finding #4009]. A related entity, Aryam Investment 1, acquired 49 percent of World Liberty Financial for $500 million four days before the presidential inauguration in January 2025, with $187 million directed to Trump family entities [Finding #3757].

MGX operates from Al Sarab Tower on Al Maryah Island in Abu Dhabi within the Abu Dhabi Global Market free zone, with a US office at One Vanderbilt Avenue in New York through MGX Fund Management (US) LLC [Finding #3991]. Its three disclosed private funds total approximately $2.42 billion in gross assets, audited by PwC and custodied at HSBC Bank Middle East Limited [Finding #3994]. Examination of the documentary record positions MGX as a structural keystone of the Tahnoon-cluster re-platforming that followed the Epstein disclosures — a single vehicle that consolidates UAE state AI capital under intelligence-aligned leadership and routes it into US technology assets, drawing on the regulatory framework set by the Brooks-era OCC interpretive letters now cited in Erebor Bank's approval [Finding #11236].

sections.title: Formation and Capital Structure
sections.content:
MGX Fund Management Limited was announced on March 12, 2024 under the Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council, established January 22, 2024 by Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed [Finding #11220]. The founding partners are Mubadala Investment Company — the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund — and G42, the Tahnoun-aligned AI champion that received a Microsoft investment in April 2024 [Finding #11220]. Three investment pillars structure the mandate: AI infrastructure (datacenters and connectivity), semiconductors, and AI core technology, with a target of $100 billion in assets under management and stated ambition for $10 billion in deals annually [Finding #11220]. The entity is organized as a private company limited by shares under UAE law and registered with the Abu Dhabi Global Market Financial Services Regulatory Authority [Finding #3991].

The SEC Form ADV filed July 22, 2025 discloses a dual ownership chain. The Mubadala chain: Government of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi (75 percent or more) holds Mubadala Investment Company PJSC, which holds Mamoura Diversified Global Holding PJSC, which holds MIC Industrial Investment 2 RSC LTD (50–75 percent), which in turn holds MGX Group Holding 1 LTD. The G42 chain: Group 42 Holding LTD (75 percent or more) holds GX Investments LTD (50–75 percent), which also holds MGX Group Holding 1 LTD [Finding #3997]. MGX Group Holding 1 LTD then holds 75 percent or more of MGX Fund Management Limited [Finding #3997]. Confidential treatment was requested for additional Schedule B ownership information under Section 210(A) of the Investment Advisers Act [Finding #3997].

The board is chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, with Khaldoon Khalifa Al Mubarak as Vice Chairman [Finding #4006]. Khaldoon's 2025 board roster — Mubadala MD/CEO, ADCB Chair, MGX Vice Chair, ADNOC, G42, Aldar, FAB, Emirates Foundation, MBZUAI Board of Trustees Chair, AIATC Secretary General, and Executive Affairs Authority Chair — places him at the simultaneous center of UAE sovereign capital, banking, real estate, and AI policy [Finding #11203]. Other directors include Jassem Al Zaabi (Chairman of the Abu Dhabi Department of Finance and Vice President of the UAE Central Bank), Peng Xiao (CEO of G42, formerly CTO of MicroStrategy), and Martin Edelman (G42 General Counsel and Of Counsel at Paul Hastings LLP) [Finding #4006]. CEO Ahmed Yahia Al Idrissi (formerly McKinsey and Mubadala Private Equity), COO/CFO Dani Dweik, and Chief Legal Officer Andre Namphy (formerly Sullivan & Cromwell, Rhodes Scholar) lead the executive team [Finding #3996]. Form ADV Section 7.A discloses 12 related general-partner entities including MGX AI Regional Infra GP 1, MGX AI Global Infra GP 1, MGX AI Tech GP 1, MGX Semis GP 1, MGX I Denali GP, and MGX Fund Management (US) LLC [Finding #4000]. The three disclosed private funds total approximately $2.42 billion in gross assets — MGX Fund I LP at $1.43 billion, MGX I Co-Investment LP at $400 million, and MGX I Denali Holding LP at $594 million in the Cayman Islands — all audited by PwC and custodied at HSBC Bank Middle East Limited [Finding #3994].

sections.title: Investment Activity
sections.content:
MGX investment activity since 2024 has concentrated on the largest US technology infrastructure transactions of the period, though public framing has frequently overstated MGX's lead role in deals where it is one partner among several. For the Stargate joint venture, The Information reports an equity split placing SoftBank at approximately 40 percent and OpenAI at approximately 40 percent, with Oracle and MGX each contributing approximately $7 billion in initial commitments [Finding #11216]. SoftBank carries financial responsibility while OpenAI carries operational responsibility under the announced division of labor [Finding #11216]. Cross-reference of the SEC primary-source filings indicates that the Stargate-MGX venture and the Klein-Altman-Oklo cluster are structurally separate transactions, despite press treatment that has frequently merged them [Finding #11236]. Records show Sam Altman resigned from the Oklo board on April 22, 2025, three months after the Stargate announcement [Finding #11236].

The Stargate announcement on January 21, 2025 was itself, on analysis of the surrounding deal flow, a re-bundling of infrastructure already in motion: Bitfury distributed a $53.9 million dividend on December 23, 2024, thirty-eight days before the Cipher PIPE; AltC closed in May 2024 with anomalous redemption activity; and Crusoe began Abilene construction in June 2024, seven months before the Stargate announcement [Finding #11236]. According to public reporting, MGX participated in OpenAI's $6.6 billion funding round in October 2025 at a $500 billion valuation, was targeted for OpenAI's $50 billion Middle East expansion alongside the Saudi Public Investment Fund, and counts among its close relationships Sam Altman, who has publicly described Sheikh Tahnoon as a dear personal friend [Finding #3771].

In September 2024, MGX co-founded the AI Infrastructure Partnership with BlackRock and Microsoft as a $30 billion equity fund, with Nvidia providing technical expertise [Finding #4009]. Through this consortium, MGX participated in the $40 billion acquisition of Aligned Data Centers in October 2025 [Finding #4009]. MGX co-led Anthropic's $30 billion Series G in February 2026 at a $380 billion valuation, alongside Coatue Management, Founders Fund, and others [Finding #4009]. Additional positions include Databricks ($10 billion round) and xAI ($6 billion round) [Finding #4009].

In December 2025, the Trump administration approved the TikTok US restructuring, in which MGX, Oracle, and Silver Lake each acquired approximately 15 percent stakes in the new US entity controlling TikTok, Lemon8, and CapCut, with ByteDance retaining 19.9 percent [Finding #4009]. The deal closed in January 2026, placing an entity controlled by the UAE National Security Adviser in partial ownership of a social media platform used by approximately 170 million Americans [Finding #4009].

sections.title: WLFI / USD1 / Binance Settlement Route
sections.content:
In March 2025 MGX invested $2 billion in Binance — described, according to financial reporting, as the first institutional investment in the exchange and the largest investment ever fully settled in cryptocurrency [Finding #3762] [Finding #3837]. In May 2025, Zachary Witkoff — CEO of World Liberty Financial and son of Trump Special Envoy Steve Witkoff — disclosed at the Token2049 conference in Dubai that the settlement was conducted using WLFI's USD1 stablecoin [Finding #3837]. According to the Warren-Merkley Senate investigation, WLFI confirmed MGX and Binance would have used foreign fiat currency had USD1 been unavailable, indicating that the Trump family was incorporated into a transaction that otherwise would not have involved them [Finding #3837] [Finding #11236].

As of February 2026, Binance held approximately 87 percent of all USD1 in circulation, valued at approximately $4.7 billion [Finding #3779]. Binance, according to Bloomberg and the Wall Street Journal, assisted in building the USD1 technology [Finding #3762]. Analysis of the financial structure identifies a circular flow whereby Tahnoon's Aryam Investment 1 pays $500 million for 49 percent of WLFI, generating $187 million for Trump family entities; Tahnoon's MGX invests $2 billion in Binance using USD1, generating demand for the stablecoin; Binance becomes the primary custodian of USD1 supply; and Trump pardons Binance founder Changpeng Zhao in October 2025 [Finding #3762]. The Warren-Merkley investigation estimated that the reserves backing USD1 could generate a potential $80 million annual yield to Trump entities [Finding #3837].

Records show the Brooks-era OCC interpretive letters #1170 and #1174, together with IL #1184, remain operative law cited in the Erebor Bank approval letter — the deregulatory framework that scaffolds WLFI and Tahnoon-cluster flows [Finding #11236]. Examination of the documented sequence shows Adam Cohen's 65-day path from Skadden through the OCC to the Erebor approval — the tightest of the documented revolving-door instances among the firms involved — completing the regulatory layer that USD1 settlement now operates inside [Finding #11236]. On February 23, 2026, WLFI reported a coordinated attack involving compromised co-founder accounts, short positions on the WLFI token, and a paid disinformation campaign; the WLFI token dropped approximately 7 percent and USD1 briefly lost its dollar peg at $0.994 before recovering [Finding #3779].

sections.title: Cross-Network Position
sections.content:
Cross-reference of the filings shows the earlier "Mubadala unifies" model expanding into a three-pillar Supreme Council for Financial and Economic Affairs sovereign architecture comprising ADIA, Mubadala, and L'IMAD — the latter formed January 2026 with approximately $300 billion in consolidated assets under Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed [Finding #11236]. Above this capital layer, the analysis indicates, sit a regulatory layer and a US-listing layer, both staffed by the same handful of cross-cutting personalities [Finding #11236].

Mohamed Ali Al Shorafa Al Hammadi occupies the regulatory layer, simultaneously holding chair positions at Hub71, the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange, the Abu Dhabi Investment Office, Etihad Aviation, the Securities and Commodities Authority, Abu Dhabi Housing, and the Department of Municipalities and Transport, with a Vice Chair seat at Abu Dhabi Global Market [Finding #11209]. His ADGM Vice Chair role is structurally significant for MGX, because Al Sarab Tower, MGX's headquarters, sits inside the ADGM free zone he helps govern, and the MGX-related general-partner entities ending in "RSC LTD" are restricted-scope companies registered in the same regulatory perimeter [Finding #11209] [Finding #4000].

The US-listing layer routes through Essa Kazim, who replaced Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem as DP World Chairman on February 13, 2026 and concurrently holds a Nasdaq Inc. board seat through Borse Dubai [Finding #11183]. The leadership change, on examination of the timing, preserved US capital-market access through personnel substitution: bin Sulayem's departure followed the February 2026 release of DOJ Epstein files containing Bloomberg-reported correspondence between bin Sulayem and Epstein, while Kazim's board seat extends, and arguably strengthens, the network's reach into US listing infrastructure [Finding #11183] [Finding #11236].

Within MGX itself, board cross-membership compounds the same architecture. Martin Edelman serves simultaneously as MGX board member, G42 General Counsel, and Of Counsel at Paul Hastings LLP; he signed the Aryam Investment 1 agreement to acquire 49 percent of World Liberty Financial and subsequently joined the WLFI board without public disclosure [Finding #4002]. Peng Xiao co-signed the same agreement and took a WLFI board seat [Finding #4002]. Records indicate Khaldoon Al Mubarak previously interfaced with the Epstein network; an October 2017 email [EFTA02586299] shows Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed delegated cryptocurrency and technology matters to Khaldoon via Mubadala [Finding #3863]. On that record, analysis suggests the same Mubadala and MBZ power structure that interfaced with the Epstein network now consolidates into MGX [Finding #3863].

sections.title: Network Continuity Through the bin Sulayem Inflection
sections.content:
The February 13, 2026 resignation of Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem as DP World Chairman, following Bloomberg reporting on his Epstein-era correspondence, marked, according to the documentary record, the first visible loss for the Tahnoon network on Epstein-related exposure [Finding #11183] [Finding #11236]. Analysis of the response shows the loss absorbed without structural damage to MGX, as the network executed personnel substitution at the apex, with Kazim replacing bin Sulayem, while the parent vehicle, the regulatory layer, and the capital pillars remained intact [Finding #11236].

The substitution mechanics suggest the bridges were designed to outlast the loss of any single principal. Kazim's board seat on Nasdaq Inc., held through Borse Dubai, preserved US capital-market access at precisely the moment a US-facing controversy threatened to remove it, the record shows [Finding #11183] [Finding #11236]. MGX itself faced no governance change during the episode: the chair (Tahnoon), vice chair (Khaldoon), board (Edelman, Xiao, Al Zaabi), and executive team (Yahia, Dweik, Namphy) remained unchanged across the February 2026 inflection point [Finding #4006] [Finding #11203]. Cross-reference of the episode places the pattern — a parent vehicle surviving the loss of an adjacent principal through pre-positioned successor architecture — within the controlled-detachment model [Finding #11236].

sections.title: Regulatory Footprint and Congressional Scrutiny
sections.content:
Despite participating in transactions that, in headline terms, exceed $100 billion in aggregate, MGX maintains a minimal direct US regulatory footprint. The fund has no GLEIF Legal Entity Identifier registration, which is standard for entities engaged in over-the-counter derivatives and major financial transactions under ESMA and SEC requirements [Finding #3786]. It has no direct SEC CIK number and files only as an exempt reporting adviser through Form ADV [Finding #3783]. A review of the records in Florida, Nevada, and New York returned no MGX registrations beyond the Delaware-formed MGX Fund Management US LLC entity [Finding #3818]. The Form ADV reports that all fund investors are non-US persons and that the entity did not have $1 billion or more in assets on its balance sheet, despite participating in transactions totaling multiples of that figure [Finding #3991].

According to congressional correspondence, Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jeff Merkley sent letters to the MGX and Binance CEOs on May 14, 2025, demanding document preservation and records on whether Trump or WLFI affiliates influenced the selection of USD1 for the Binance settlement [Finding #3790].
